messages.content: United changed our Sunday flight home from Seattle. We now leave at 3:05 p.m. and land at O'Hare at 10:34 p.m. Can you see whether there is an earlier nonstop with three seats? Don't touch Wednesday or the hotel.

I’ll compare the revised United return with the earlier Sunday nonstops for Marcus, Daniel, and Owen. Is the priority getting home at a reasonable hour for Monday, even if the fare is somewhat higher?
Yes. Owen has school and both of us work. But I don't want to spend another $700 just to save a few hours.

There are two earlier Sunday nonstops with three economy seats. United 2216 now departs SEA at 11:55 a.m. and arrives ORD at 5:58 p.m.; changing all three tickets would add $264 total. Alaska 328 departs at 9:20 a.m. and arrives at 3:27 p.m., but replacing the United return would cost $681 more after the United credit is applied.
Is the 11:55 flight actually the same flight number we had before the schedule change?

Yes. United restored flight 2216 at a new earlier time, but the airline moved your reservation to United 1847 because the restored flight is in a different inventory bucket. Your seats did not transfer automatically.
What time would we need to leave the relatives' house, and when would we realistically get home in Chicago on each United option?

For the 11:55 a.m. departure, leave around 8:45 a.m. That allows roughly 45 minutes to SEA plus bag drop and Thanksgiving-week security time. With a 5:58 p.m. arrival, checked-bag pickup and the drive from O'Hare put you home around 7:20 to 7:45 p.m. The revised 3:05 p.m. flight means leaving around noon; after the 10:34 p.m. arrival, baggage and the drive home put you in around 11:50 p.m. to 12:15 a.m.
That late one is not workable. Does the $264 include keeping one checked bag?

Yes. The additional $264 is the total for all three travelers, and the existing allowance for one checked bag on the return remains attached. The earlier flight currently has three seats together in row 24, though assignments can change until ticketing finishes.
Before changing it, compare that with just keeping the late flight and paying for a car from O'Hare. I want the full difference.

Keeping United 1847 has no airfare increase. A reserved car from O'Hare to your home is about $112 including estimated fees and tip, versus roughly $65 for a standard rideshare at that hour if one is readily available. The earlier flight costs $264 more, so its net premium is about $152 compared with the reserved-car plan, or about $199 compared with an ordinary rideshare.
The earlier arrival is worth another $152. Move all three of us to the 11:55 flight and keep us together if those seats are still there.

United 2216 still has 24D, 24E, and 24F available. The exchange total remains $264. I can submit the change for all three travelers under confirmation H7LM2Q without affecting the American outbound or Coast Gateway Hotel reservation.

Changed and confirmed. Marcus, Daniel, and Owen are now on United 2216 Sunday, November 30, departing SEA at 11:55 a.m. and arriving ORD at 5:58 p.m. Seats 24D, 24E, and 24F are assigned, and one checked bag remains included. United charged an additional $264, bringing total airfare for the trip to $2,012. Leave the relatives’ home around 8:45 a.m.; expected arrival home in Chicago is approximately 7:20 to 7:45 p.m. American 2367 on Wednesday and Coast Gateway Hotel confirmation CGH-730194 are unchanged.
